whenToUse: The all-round friendly hello with anyone you call ты: friends, classmates, colleagues your age. With older strangers or a boss, use Здравствуйте instead.
A warm, slightly loud greeting between guys or close friends. It also means "great!", so listen to the tone. Too casual for formal situations.
example: Здорово, братан! Сто лет не виделись!

whenToUse: A breezy, slightly retro hello or goodbye among friends. Cheerful and safe, but you won't hear it from older people very often.
Чё is the street version of что. Great with friends, strange with your boss or a stranger. A normal answer is Норм, а у тебя?
The Swiss army knife of Russian. It ends phone calls (Ну давай!), agrees to plans and urges people on. Safe everywhere with people you call ты.
The standard lazy answer to how are you. Fine with friends and in chats; in a formal email write нормально instead.
Praise that works for almost anything: a gig, a new phone, a good story. Safe with all ages, a bit casual for a formal speech.
example: Круто! Я тоже хочу такой телефон.

whenToUse: Friendly and young-sounding. It can mean fun, funny or just interesting. Fine with friends and colleagues, a bit casual with a boss.
The polite swear: it sounds like the stronger word but is totally safe. Said by kids, parents and teachers alike when something goes wrong. A good one to start with.
Mild and common, a bit old-fashioned. Fine in most casual situations, though some older or religious people may wince. Not for a job interview.
A softened, slangy stand-in for the much ruder пиздец. Everyone uses it, but it is still crude, so keep it with friends and peers, not parents or bosses.
Young slang for something extreme, good or bad: a wild party, an awful exam, a crazy price. Safe among peers, odd in formal talk.
example: Вчера была жесть, я еле дошёл домой.

whenToUse: A mild swear (from фиг, a polite stand-in for the worse word). Common and good-humoured, but still slangy; skip it with older relatives or at work.
Casual and mild: that's rubbish, no big deal. Fine among friends. A polite-ish stand-in for херня.
example: Да ладно, это фигня, не переживай.

whenToUse: Relaxed word for a guy, like dude. Fine among peers; it can sound rude or too familiar toward older strangers.
Texting shorthand for спасибо. Fine in chats with friends and colleagues; it can feel curt toward someone you barely know.
Texting shorthand for пожалуйста. Also written пжлст. Chat-only; never in a formal message or email.
Texting shorthand: оч круто, оч устал. Chat-only, with friends. You will not hear it spoken often.
How сейчас sounds in fast speech, also written ща in chats. Perfectly normal among friends. Beware: щас can mean "in a bit" too.
Chat shorthand that hides a rude phrase (хрен знает). Everyone uses it with friends, but don't send it to a boss or a teacher.
example: — Во сколько начало? — Хз, спроси Диму.

whenToUse: Texting shorthand for может быть. Chat-only, with friends.
Gamer slang from "go". Used for quick plans among friends: Го в кино? Use with peers only.
Used in Russian chats exactly as in English, even spoken aloud with a Russian accent. Safe among friends.
Mildly insulting. Between close friends it's playful; to a stranger, or in anger, it is a real insult. Never to your boss.
example: Ну ты дурак! Я чуть не упал.

whenToUse: A clear insult, stronger than дурак. A joke only between very close friends; in an argument it will start a fight.
example: Он такой идиот, сам себя запер в квартире.

whenToUse: Literally horseradish. As a stand-in for a ruder word: Какого хрена? = what the hell? Crude, but a notch below real мат; keep it with friends.
example: Какого хрена ты мне не позвонил?

whenToUse: Real мат: very strong and vulgar, though common among adults for anything extreme, good or bad. Never with parents, elders, at work or around children. Recognise it; don't use it casually.
The heaviest everyday swear word, the real thing behind блин. Everyone hears it, but it is highly offensive in public, at work or in front of elders and kids. Only with very close friends, if at all.
example: Блядь, я забыл телефон в такси!

whenToUse: Very strong and aggressive. Said of a person it is a serious insult; as an exclamation (Вот сука!) it is rude venting. Avoid it in nearly every situation.

english: the hell with it / get lost
whenToUse: Strong and rude: Иди нахрен! means go to hell. Used to dismiss someone or something; can start a fight. Friends may joke with it, nobody else should.
example: Да ну его нахрен, этот проект!

whenToUse: A hostile brush-off, softer than the full мат versions but still seriously rude. Never to someone you want to stay on good terms with.
example: Пошёл ты, я не буду это делать!
